record.paper_title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem
record.original_question: In the same n by n input-queued switch model with load factor ρ(λ) and optimal steady-state expected total queue size Q*(n,λ), what is β*_1, the infimum over positive β for which there is a constant c > 0 such that, for every fixed n, the heavy-traffic limit superior as ρ(λ) approaches 1 of (1 − ρ(λ)) Q*(n,λ) is at most c n^β? Is the value of this exponent 1?

evidence.quote: Find β∗1, the infimum over all positive numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that lim sup ρ(λ)→1 (1 − ρ(λ)) · Q∗(n,λ) ≤ c · nβ.
an intermediate (weaker) conjecture, such as β∗1 = 1, may be easier to prove.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an $n \times n$ input-queued switch operating in discrete time. There are $n$ input ports and $n$ output ports, and for each pair $(i,j) \in \{1,\dots,n\}^2$ a queue $Q_{ij}$ that stores packets arriving at input $i$ destined to output $j$. In each time slot, independent Bernoulli arrivals occur with rate matrix $\lambda = (\lambda_{ij})$ where $\lambda_{ij} \ge 0$. The load factor is
$$\rho(\lambda) \;=\; \max\!\left\{\max_{i}\sum_{j}\lambda_{ij},\ \max_{j}\sum_{i}\lambda_{ij}\right\},$$
and we assume $\rho(\lambda) < 1$. A scheduling policy chooses, at each time slot, a matching (permutation matrix) $\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ and serves one packet from $Q_{ij}$ whenever $\sigma_{ij}=1$ and $Q_{ij}>0$. For any scheduling policy that yields a positive-recurrent Markov chain on the queue-length state, let
$$Q(n,\lambda) \;=\; \limsup_{t\to\infty} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{i,j} Q_{ij}(t)\right],$$
and define
$$Q^{*}(n,\lambda) \;=\; \inf\{\,Q(n,\lambda):\text{stable scheduling policies}\,\}.$$

Define
$$\beta^{*}_{1} \;=\; \inf\Big\{\beta > 0 : \exists\, c>0 \text{ such that for every fixed } n,\ \limsup_{\rho(\lambda)\to 1}\, \bigl(1-\rho(\lambda)\bigr)\,Q^{*}(n,\lambda) \le c\, n^{\beta}\Big\}.$$

Determine $\beta^{*}_{1}$. In particular, is $\beta^{*}_{1} = 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Maguluri and Srikant (Stochastic Systems, 2016) proved that under the MaxWeight policy with uniform Bernoulli arrivals, the heavy-traffic limit $\lim_{\rho\to 1}(1-\rho)\,\mathbb{E}[\sum Q_{ij}] = n - 3/2 + 1/(2n)$, hence $O(n)$ for fixed $n$. Since $Q^*\le Q_{\text{MaxWeight}}$ and a matching $\Omega(n)$ lower bound on the workload holds, this yields $\beta^{*}_{1}=1$. Subsequent works (e.g., Maguluri–Burle–Srikant on incompletely saturated switches) extended the optimal $O(n)$ heavy-traffic scaling to broader arrival regimes. The weaker conjecture $\beta^{*}_{1}=1$ is therefore established. The stronger joint-scaling conjecture $Q^*=O(n/(1-\rho))$ for all $n$ and $\rho<1$ remains an active research direction (with the best known general bound improved by Xu–Zhong via graph factorization).

status_evidence.title: Heavy traffic queue length behavior in a switch under the MaxWeight algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Heavy-traffic scaled queue length is $(1-1/(2n))\|\sigma\|^2$; in uniform Bernoulli case equals $n-3/2+1/(2n)$, showing optimal scaling with respect to $n$, settling an open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that for fixed $n$, $(1-\rho)\mathbb{E}[\sum Q_{ij}]$ scales as $\Theta(n)$ under MaxWeight, implying $\beta^*_1 = 1$.

status_evidence.title: Optimal heavy-traffic queue length scaling in an incompletely saturated switch
status_evidence.snippet: Heavy-traffic queue length under MaxWeight has optimal scaling with respect to switch size in incompletely saturated regimes.

status_evidence.title: Improved queue-size scaling for input-queued switches via graph factorization
status_evidence.claim: Progress on the stronger joint $(n,\rho)$ scaling conjecture; consistent with $\beta^*_1=1$ in the heavy-traffic-first limit.
